title: POC scoping: commercial guardrails / pilot terms
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-12
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~60m
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Karen (Summit Head of AI), Omar (Platform Eng), Priya (Procurement), Mike (CTO)

Summary:
Quick POC scoping to align on success criteria, workload sizing, benchmark plan, timeline, and the commercial guardrails. AE+SE from Redwood on call; procurement present to confirm commercial constraints.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call: Maya Thompson, Redwood AE. Diego from our SE team.
[00:12] Diego: Hi all. I'll be driving the technical scoping piece.
[00:17] Karen: Karen here, Head of AI at Summit. Omar and Priya and Mike are on as well.
[00:22] Mike: yes, hi.
[00:25] Maya: Great. Agenda: success criteria for the POC, what workloads you'll run, what benchmarks we should run, timeline, and the commercial guardrails — credits, pilot term, and then path to procurement. Sound good?
[00:38] Karen: Yep that's perfect. We're trying to validate cost/latency for a summarization + reranking pipeline and an embedding-based search workload. Primary success criteria are: 1) 99th percentile latency under 350ms for short prompt completion on dedicated capacity, 2) cost per 1k queries better than our current infra by 30%, and 3) no data residency/exfil concerns; logs should be retained per our policy.
[01:05] Diego: Good. When you say 350ms 99p, is that tail for host inference or dedicated GPUs? Which model size are you planning to use?
[01:12] Karen: We were thinking a mix: a 7B quantized model for search/embeds and 13B for summarization. For latency target we want dedicated for the critical path but also want to benchmark hosted API fallback.
[01:30] Diego: OK. For 7B on our dedicated pools we usually see sub-200ms p50 and ~220-300ms p99 depending on batching and sequence length. For 13B p99 can be in the 400-800ms range unless we tune batching and KV cache. We can run a couple of benchmarks with your typical input size.
[01:49] Omar: Our average prompt length for summarization is ~120 tokens; for search it's short — 16-32 tokens to encode query. We also do 512-token context for some medical notes.
[02:02] Diego: 512 context changes things; memory and KV cache matter. We'll include a 512 token run in the benchmark matrix.
[02:10] Maya: On the commercial side, we offer pilot credits for POCs: typical starter is $10k in credits over 30-45 days for feature-level validation; for more involved infra-style benchmarks we can extend to $25k and up depending on scope.
[02:28] Priya: From procurement: we need the pilot to have clear scope so we can avoid early contractual commitments. Also need to know if any data left the VPC or was persisted in Redwood logs. What are the retention and deletion options?
[02:42] Diego: For Private deployments, customer controls KMS and logging; for Dedicated we mask logs and provide audit logs with configurable retention; hosted API keeps minimal transient logs unless enabled — we can share SOC2/ISO docs.
[02:55] Maya: We'll share the security pack after the call. That's standard.

[03:05] Karen: For success criteria: beyond latency/cost, we need output quality parity: ROUGE/compression or a small human eval comparing outputs to our baseline. How would you suggest we run that?
[03:18] Diego: We recommend a gold set of 200-500 examples for each task. We can run automatic metrics (ROUGE, BLEU for summarization is rough) and couple that with a blind human A/B of ~50 samples to catch hallucination/regression. We can instrument scoring in our benchmark harness and return per-run metrics.
[03:36] Omar: We already have a test set for 7B; I'll share it.
[03:40] Maya: Great. Timeline: how long to spin up the POC and run benchmarks?
[03:46] Diego: If it's Dedicated or Private, provisioning can take 3-5 business days after infra sign-off for dedicated pools; hosted API is immediate. End-to-end benchmark runs typically 7-10 days including QA and human evals. So I'd budget 2-3 weeks from kickoff for actionable results.
[04:02] Priya: From procurement standpoint, the pilot term — you said 30-45 days credits? We prefer a 45-day window to capture week-to-week traffic variance. Also, what happens to credits if we exceed them?
[04:15] Maya: We can do 45 days. Credits cover usage up to the amount; if you exceed, we'd flag you and the excess is billed at a negotiated pilot rate; typically a discounted list rate; or we pause until you confirm. We can put a hard spend cap so no surprise bills.
[04:31] Priya: We need a cap. Please make that explicit in the pilot agreement.
[04:35] Maya: Absolutely. We'll include a hard cap and notifications.

[04:42] Mike: Path to procurement: what is typical conversion to a contract if the POC is successful? Do we need NDA/CSP? Who signs?
[04:51] Maya: Typically, after a successful pilot we surface a SOW or dedicated capacity agreement. For Dedicated/Private we move to an enterprise contract with monthly commit or annual, and include SLAs. Procurement signs master services agreement + SOW. NDAs are separate; most customers already have one in place. We'll work with your legal.
[05:06] Priya: Timeline wise procurement needs 2-3 weeks once terms are agreed. Pricing review will go to finance.

[05:14] Diego: Back to benchmarks: can you confirm expected QPS and concurrency for the two workloads?
[05:19] Karen: For search/embed: baseline 50 QPS sustained with spikes to 200 QPS. Summarization: lower QPS, maybe 10-20 QPS but higher compute per request. We also want concurrency tests with 50-100 concurrent small requests.
[05:34] Diego: Good. We'll include sustained and spike scenarios. For autoscaling on Dedicated we can show cold/warm node behavior and warm-up time.
[05:42] Omar: For the embedding workload we also want evaluation of vector index refreshes — we do daily bulk upserts ~100k vectors and need ingestion performance.
[05:52] Diego: We'll run a bulk index ingest benchmark using your vector sizes; provide expected vector dim and indexing pipeline and we'll simulate.

[06:00] Maya: Commercial guardrails detail: 1) Pilot credits: $25k for this POC, 45-day term, hard spend cap equals credits. 2) Pilot rate card for overage: 30% discount off list. 3) No commitment required to start pilot; conversion to contract requires procurement review and SOW. 4) Support: standard email support during pilot; optional paid support add-on if you want 24/7 during heavy load.
[06:25] Priya: We also need data processing addendum and DPA terms up front. Can you send template?
[06:30] Maya: Yes, we'll attach DPA template with the security pack.

[06:36] Karen: Are there any limits on model variants we can test? We want to try quantized weights and a half-precision variant if available.
[06:45] Diego: We can provide quantized variants. On Dedicated you can pin a variant. On hosted there are some model variant limits due to capacity but we'll prioritize pilot runs.
[06:55] Karen: Great. Also, what telemetry do we get: per-token cost, per-route latency?
[07:01] Diego: Redwood Console will show token-level cost, p50/p95/p99 latency, per-model route breakdown and tracing. We'll grant you a view for the pilot.

[07:10] Maya: Ok let's confirm final success criteria as discussed: 1) p99 latency <350ms for 7B in dedicated during typical load, 2) cost reduction >=30% vs current infra for the same QPS, 3) ingestion throughput for vectors >=100k/day with acceptable indexing latency, 4) output quality parity within predefined thresholds, and 5) clear data residency controls and DPA signed.
[07:36] Mike: That reads good. We'll circulate an internal sign-off matrix.

[07:45] Karen: On inputs, I'll share two data sets: short queries (search) and 200 long-form summarization examples plus 50 audit samples for human eval. Omar will share vector format and indexing jobs.
[07:58] Omar: Will do by EOD tomorrow.

[08:02] Maya: Next: deliverables and who does what.
[08:06] Diego: Redwood will: 1) spin up a dedicated pilot pool (once infra OK), 2) run benchmarks (latency/cost/ingest) per provided datasets, 3) run automated metrics and coordinate a 50-sample human A/B, 4) provide dashboard access and a benchmark report.
[08:22] Maya: Summit will: provide datasets, define cost baseline (current infra numbers), sign DPA, and provide a procurement contact for contract discussions.

[08:31] Priya: For the pilot agreement: we need an explicit clause that pilot credits expire after 45 days and a hard cap will prevent charges beyond credits unless we sign off.
[08:43] Maya: We'll include that. Also include activity milestones: kickoff, provisioning complete, initial benchmark run, human eval, final report.

[08:54] Diego: Any competitors mentioned? I heard you previously ran similar tests with Anthropic and an in-house cluster?
[09:00] Karen: We piloted Anthropic via hosted for chat features; we also run self-hosted on GKE for batch jobs.
[09:07] Maya: Noted.

[09:10] Priya: Procurement question: do you require a minimum term if we convert to Dedicated? We prefer monthly commits but willing to discuss annual.
[09:19] Maya: Typical Dedicated pricing prefers quarterly or annual commits for discounted rates, but we can do a monthly committed setup for a transition period. We'll surface options in the SOW.

[09:31] Mike: Alright, can we get something in writing with the credit amount, cap, deliverables and timeline?
[09:37] Maya: Yes — I'll send a pilot summary (SOW-lite) and the security pack + DPA. We'll propose $25k credits, 45 days, hard cap, and a 3-week benchmark window after provisioning.

[09:51] Karen: Sounds good. A couple more clarifying Qs: who owns the benchmark infra costs for private deployment?
[09:58] Diego: For Private we don't manage the underlying infra; it's customer-managed. For Dedicated it's included in Redwood's managed pool under the pilot credits. If you opt to run Private on-prem, you'd cover compute but we can advise on sizing.

[10:12] Priya: OK. Please send a template SLR (service level request) and SOW-lite. Procurement needs those to start internal approvals.

[10:20] Maya: Got it. Any other outstanding items?
[10:23] Karen: No, just the timeline alignment: let's tentatively aim to kick off next Monday if procurement clears.
[10:29] Maya: Perfect. We'll target next Monday.

[10:33] Maya: Recap of action items and next steps: I'll share in chat. Thanks everyone.

Action items (in transcript body):
- Diego: Prepare benchmark matrix and provisional cluster sizing; will include 7B/13B runs + 512-token tests.
- Omar: Share datasets (search, summarization) and vector specs by EOD tomorrow.
- Maya: Send pilot SOW-lite (credits $25k, 45d), security pack, DPA, and pilot agreement with hard cap.
- Priya: Provide procurement calendar and legal contact info.

End of transcript.
summary: POC scoping meeting to agree success criteria (latency, cost, ingestion, output quality), workload sizing (7B/13B models, 512-token context, QPS/concurrency, vector ingests), benchmark plan, timeline (~2-3 weeks for results), and commercial guardrails (pilot credits $25k, 45 days, hard spend cap, overage pricing, path to procurement). Redwood to provide SOW-lite, security pack and run benchmarks; customer to provide datasets and procurement details.
